senses.definition: (transitive) To affect (someone) strongly and often favourably.
examples: You impressed me with your command of Urdu.

quotes.text: Mr. Campion appeared suitably impressed and she warmed to him. He was very easy to talk to with those long clown lines in his pale face, a natural goon, born rather too early she suspected.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To make an impression, to be impressive.
examples: Henderson impressed in his first game as captain.

quotes.text: Manchester United's Tom Cleverley impressed on his first competitive start and Lampard demonstrated his continued worth at international level in a performance that was little more than a stroll once England swiftly exerted their obvious authority.
quotes.reference: 2012 September 7, Phil McNulty, “Moldova 0-5 England”, in BBC Sport:

senses.definition: (transitive) To produce a vivid impression of (something).
examples: That first view of the Eiger impressed itself on my mind.

senses.definition: (transitive) To mark or stamp (something) using pressure.
examples: We impressed our footprints in the wet cement.

senses.definition: To produce (a mark, stamp, image, etc.); to imprint (a mark or figure upon something).
(figurative) To fix deeply in the mind; to present forcibly to the attention, etc.; to imprint; to inculcate.

quotes.text: impress the motives and methods of persuasion upon our own hearts, till we feel the force and power of them.

senses.definition: (transitive) To compel (someone) to serve in a military force.
examples: The press gang used to impress people into the Navy.

senses.definition: (transitive) To seize or confiscate (property) by force.
examples: The liner was impressed as a troop carrier.
